true_answer: When this does not occur (that is, when each element of the codomain is the image of at most one element of the domain) then we say the function is one-to-one . Again, this terminology makes sense: we are sending at most one element from the domain to one element from the codomain. One input to one output. The fancy math term for a one-to-one function is an injection . We call one-to-one functions injective functions. In pictures: Injective Not injective Example 0.4.7 Which functions are injective (i.e., one-to-one)? 1. f : Z → Z defined by f ( n ) | 3 n .
